PullRequest.Title: sessions: Add Test App and persistent Retest actions
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Adds **Test App / Retest App** above the Agents Window composer so users can request UI verification after an agent builds or changes an app.

## Demos

Testing and retesting a multi-page Mini Store app.

### Test App

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c3167913-112d-4570-bb32-0565650d0b99

### Retest App

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff05e0f5-4abb-4622-a2a2-81aeb8aaf4f6

## How it works

- **Appears after UI work:** uses changed files and project hints to show the button after a successful turn with likely UI changes.
- **Requests UI testing:** asks the agent to launch the app, check the relevant flows, fix issues, and retest using its existing tools.
- **Remembers previous requests:** after a testing request is accepted, the label becomes Retest App. This is remembered per chat across restarts—not a guarantee that tests passed.
- **Stays contextual:** hidden while the agent is working or when the latest turn has no qualifying UI changes, including test-only turns without edits.

## Validation

- 250 focused unit tests passed.
- Client type-checking and targeted ESLint passed.
- 14 component fixtures rendered and disposed without errors, covering initial/retest states, narrow layouts, light/dark, and high contrast.
- Verified the updated single-button implementation in a running Code OSS Agents Window.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The unique key construction, profile lifetime, lack of any removal reference, and available deletion lifecycle are directly established in the changed and surrounding code. The exact number of affected profiles is uncertain, but retention grows deterministically with distinct tested chats.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Persistent profile-storage rows, in-memory key-target entries, and serialized key-target bytes
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Retained state grows O(N) with the number of distinct chats ever tested, including deleted chats; because adding a new target rewrites the full key-target JSON object, cumulative metadata serialization across N additions grows O(N²).
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Unbounded retained memory/disk and progressively more profile-storage serialization/startup work
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this change, Test App history did not exist, so using and later deleting agent chats added no persistent profile-storage entries.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every accepted Test App request now creates a distinct profile-storage key derived from the chat resource, and the new component never removes or bounds those keys.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 120 calls `storageService.store` with a key containing the unique session resource; no changed code removes that key or imposes a cap.
Findings.Title: Prune per-chat Test App storage when chats disappear
Findings.Impact: Profiles that use Test App across many chats retain every chat URI after those chats are deleted. The retained rows and storage target metadata grow for the lifetime of the profile, increasing profile-storage memory/disk usage and the cost of loading and updating that metadata.
Findings.Evidence: The added callback stores `sessions.testApp.requested.${getComparisonKey(resource)}` for each accepted chat. Repository search finds no removal for this prefix. `ISessionsManagementService` exposes `onDidDeleteSession`/`onDidDeleteChat`, and nearby `SessionArchiveNudgeService` explicitly removes per-session persisted state on deletion, but this component does not subscribe to lifecycle cleanup. `AbstractStorageService.updateKeyTarget` also serializes the complete key-target object whenever a new key is added, so stale keys affect both retained bytes and subsequent storage updates.
Findings.Recommendation: Persist this flag in chat-owned metadata that is deleted with the chat, or centralize it in a bounded record that removes entries on chat/session deletion and draft/session replacement (and prunes orphaned entries at startup).

Scenarios.Scenario: A completed agent turn is evaluated for whether Test App should appear
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Synchronous diff/path classification runs when the response becomes complete. If direct UI-file matching fails, manifest reads must finish before the button can appear, but chat completion and composer usability do not wait for them.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and parse package.json or pubspec.yaml to infer whether ordinary source changes belong to a UI project
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For each workspace folder containing relevant changed source files, at most one package.json read for JS/TS and one pubspec.yaml read for Dart; folders and the two manifest types are processed sequentially.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No Test App classification or manifest reads occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only delays optional button visibility; it is off the chat response/composer critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of changed files times workspace folders for path classification, then the number of workspace folders containing JS/TS or Dart changes for manifest reads; effective boundary cardinality is at most two reads per qualifying folder.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Manifest reads are serialized by nested loops and await; no burst is created.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Direct UI extensions avoid reads. There is no component-level positive, negative, or in-flight manifest cache, so a later observable reevaluation can read again; the response-diff provider itself memoizes request observables. Cold and warm filesystem behavior otherwise depends on IFileService.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the synchronous loops and exact read cardinality are explicit in the changed code and tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large multi-root sessions or repeated post-completion reevaluations are possible, but typical turns touch few roots and the work gates only an optional control, so the observed mechanism does not justify a separate finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the new boundary is deliberately scoped, sequential, avoided on fast paths, and off the main chat critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: The user activates Test App or Retest App
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The click enters ChatWidget.acceptInput, may save dirty editors and resolve existing submission preparation, then sends one chat request. The new expected-session checks are synchronous and do not add an awaited boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Save all editors through the existing saveAllBeforeChatSend path
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One save-all operation per activation, with actual writes determined by dirty editors.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Programmatic chat submissions already used the same save-before-send path; the PR adds a new explicit user action that invokes it once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before the request is sent, as for existing chat submissions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the generated testing prompt through chatService.sendRequest
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One send per accepted button activation; submission state prevents concurrent repeated clicks from this button.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: ChatWidget already sent one request per accepted submission; this feature adds a new user-triggered submission entry point.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Starts the requested agent turn and is the purpose of the action.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Store the remembered Test App flag in profile storage
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One store callback per accepted testing request; repeated tests in the same chat overwrite the same key, while each distinct chat adds a key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No per-chat Test App history was persisted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously in the acceptance callback but does not wait for the agent response.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One action per user click; the submitted prompt has fixed size. Persistent cardinality scales with distinct chats rather than clicks in the same chat.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The local submitting observable hides the action during submission, yielding one in-flight activation per view; ChatWidget retains its existing queue/cancellation semantics.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The remembered boolean is read synchronously from profile storage and shared by storage change events. Same-chat writes reuse the key; distinct chats do not coalesce.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the click path, boundary calls, and serialization behavior are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Save duration and network latency depend on dirty files and service state, but those are existing submission costs. The unbounded profile-key lifetime is deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: The request path itself is appropriately single-shot; the per-chat persistence is reportable because entries are never pruned.

Scenarios.Scenario: Chats and sessions are deleted or replaced after Test App was used
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Deletion completes through the sessions provider and lifecycle events, but no Test App cleanup runs. The stale state remains off the deletion critical path and is subsequently loaded as part of profile storage metadata.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Retain profile-storage rows and the key-target metadata entry for deleted chat resources
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One retained entry per distinct tested chat, including chats no longer present.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Deleting chats left no Test App keys because the feature and keys did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No cleanup cost is paid during deletion; retained state increases later profile-storage load and update work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize the complete storage key-target object when adding each new per-chat key
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full key-target serialization for the first Test App store in each distinct chat; serialized bytes grow with all retained profile keys.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Test App usage contributed no keys to this profile-wide object.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs during the acceptance callback for a newly tested chat.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Lifetime count of distinct tested chat resources, including deleted and replaced chats.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Lifecycle deletion and storage updates are serialized by their respective services; absence of cleanup, not concurrency, causes growth.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Profile storage keeps both values and key-target metadata. There is no pruning, cap, expiry, or orphan reconciliation for the new prefix.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: repository-wide search finds only reads/writes for the prefix, while explicit session/chat deletion events and nearby cleanup precedent exist.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The time needed to accumulate many tested chats varies by user, but retention and serialization growth are certain and profile-lifetime.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported as unbounded persistent retention with increasing storage serialization cost.

Scenarios.Scenario: The chat pet moves or the new button changes size/visibility
Scenarios.CriticalPath: When the pet queries a platform position, the registered provider contributes the visible button element and existing pet geometry code reads its bounding rectangle. Resize and visibility events can also trigger a platform-position update.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the button DOM geometry through getBoundingClientRect during chat-pet platform calculation
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional geometry read per platform query while the button is visible; existing pill elements were already queried by the same loop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only existing status-pill platform elements were measured.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs on pet positioning/throw animation frames, not chat submission.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Pet positioning frequency and visible platform element count; this PR adds one element, not an input-sized collection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Browser animation/layout work is synchronous on the UI thread; no parallel work or queue is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No geometry cache is used, but ResizeObserver provides invalidation events and the incremental measured element count is constant.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the extra DOM read; low evidence of material incremental cost.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser layout cost depends on invalidation state, but the diff adds only one read to an existing geometry pass.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: constant one-element amplification of an existing pet geometry path is insufficient to establish a material regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: A guarded programmatic submission remains bound to its originating chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new validator executes before submission and after existing awaited preparation stages. Existing save, cancellation, prompt-resolution, attachment-resolution, and send boundaries remain in their prior positions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing save-all and prompt/directory attachment resolution during chat submission
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Unchanged per submission; validation is a constant-time check after each await.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same awaited preparation boundaries ran without post-await ownership validation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing operations remain on the send critical path; the added checks only abort if ownership changed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of existing asynchronous preparation stages, which is fixed for a submission; URI equality checks do not scale with chat history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new concurrency, serialization, queue, or limiter behavior is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the complete changed call path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Negligible constant CPU overhead; no expensive resource is newly reached.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding; the added work is bounded synchronous validation around existing awaits.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 10 changed files and relevant transitive paths. One medium-confidence-impact finding was submitted for unbounded per-chat profile-storage retention and growing key-target serialization; manifest detection, guarded submission, and chat-pet geometry changes did not meet the threshold for additional findings.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
